name: Chayote
summary: A vigorous climbing cucurbit grown for edible fruit. Kew accepts Sicyos edulis and lists Sechium edule as a synonym; UF/IFAS describes warm-climate production, trellis management, pollination and whole-fruit propagation.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Sicyos edulis and lists Sechium edule as a synonym; UF/IFAS uses Sechium edule. Gardenpedia preserves both names and does not claim a named cultivar or fruit form.

cultivation.short: Warm, frost-sensitive vine; avoid waterlogged roots
cultivation.guidance: UF/IFAS summarizes tropical/subtropical growing conditions: daytime temperatures around 66–86°F and nights above 60°F are reported as favorable; frost can damage or kill the plant. It describes growth in full sun or partial shade, fertile well-drained soil, and a soil pH around 5.5–7.0. The report also notes that Florida production recommendations are not well established, so these are literature/crop-context ranges—not a guaranteed local schedule or container/hydroponic prescription. Avoid standing water; the shallow-rooted crop needs irrigation in dry periods.

growth.short: Very vigorous perennial climber; flowering and fruit set depend on context
growth.guidance: Kew describes Sicyos edulis as a liana; UF/IFAS reports stems may reach about 50 feet and recommends a substantial trellis. In the cited crop literature, flowering is associated with roughly 12-hour day length, and absence of pollinators can prevent successful fruit development. These are species/crop-level observations, not cultivar-specific timing or a small-system fit.

harvest.short: Harvest fruit after it has developed; size and form vary
harvest.guidance: UF/IFAS reports fruit development of about 35 days after pollination in its crop literature review and describes harvest selection by appearance, color, shape and freedom from decay or insect feeding. Fruit sizes and shapes vary widely among regions and forms, so the timing is not a cultivar-specific maturity guarantee. The guide describes early-morning harvest for firmer tissues in its commercial crop context.

maintenance.short: Train the vine on a sturdy trellis
maintenance.guidance: UF/IFAS recommends a substantial trellis—commonly around 6 feet in its Florida crop guide—and positions it to allow access beneath the vine. Trellis height is support guidance, not a mature plant height or recommendation for a countertop appliance or small container.

problems.short: Dry-season mites and fruit injury can compromise growth and harvest
problems.guidance: UF/IFAS reports spider mites as a dry-season threat, with yellow leaves and fruit scabbing as recognizable signs. It also describes insects that perforate young fruit and root-damaging nematodes. These are crop-context risks, not a diagnosis or a cultivar-resistance claim; the source does not establish a universal home treatment.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: The source is crop and outdoor-truss guidance, not a validated home hydroponic system trial.

growthHabits.reason: Climbing habit is explicit, but the controlled vocabulary does not establish system fit.

height.reason: The source-reported 50-foot vine extent is not vertical mature plant height under a defined support/training setup.

spread.reason: Vine extent depends on training and is not a finite indoor spread value.

spacing.reason: Outdoor hills and trellis spacing are not transferred to pod or machine layouts.

light.reason: Full sun and partial-shade outdoor contexts do not establish an indoor grow-light tier.

name: Waterleaf
summary: A warm-climate leafy vegetable also known as Ceylon or Surinam spinach. Kew accepts Talinum fruticosum and treats T. triangulare as a synonym. Kew records an annual life form, while UF/IFAS describes a short-lived perennial crop in Florida and Singapore NParks records perennial lifespan in Singapore. These source contexts do not establish one universal lifespan or overwintering guarantee.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Talinum fruticosum and includes Talinum triangulare as a synonym; the UF/IFAS crop guide uses the latter name interchangeably. This profile follows Kew's accepted name while recording the source's taxonomy scope.

cultivation.short: Warm-season leafy crop; bright outdoor light and free-draining soil
cultivation.guidance: UF/IFAS gives Florida crop and container context. Singapore NParks recommends about 4–8 hours of direct sun or at least 6 hours of indirect outdoor light, in loamy, well-drained potting soil at least 10 cm deep. These are regional outdoor/container recommendations; they do not establish indoor grow-light tiers, a universal climate calendar or hydroponic suitability.

growth.short: Erect succulent herb; lifespan descriptions are context-specific
growth.guidance: Kew records the accepted species as annual. UF/IFAS describes waterleaf as an erect perennial herb in its Florida crop guidance, while also calling it short-lived and reporting a 30–45-day planting-to-first-harvest period. Singapore NParks records perennial lifespan in Singapore. The profile preserves each source's context rather than choosing a universal lifespan; these sources do not establish overwintering performance for a user's climate. UF/IFAS cites 3–10 feet, while NParks gives 0.3–1 m; these regional/crop dimensions are not assigned as an indoor compatibility size.

harvest.short: Harvest shoots repeatedly; cut stems near the ground
harvest.guidance: UF/IFAS reports that shoot harvest can begin about 3–4 weeks after planting and recur at 1–2 week intervals for up to two months in its Florida crop context. It recommends cutting stems about 1 inch above the ground and reports declining yield after roughly four harvests. Singapore NParks describes harvest from about 40–55 days after sowing through a period of up to six months, at two-week intervals. These are regional crop observations, not a cultivar-specific or indoor schedule; UF/IFAS also notes early-morning harvest for freshness.

maintenance.short: Stem cuttings are a practical propagation route
maintenance.guidance: UF/IFAS describes 5–8 inch mature-stem cuttings planted directly into prepared beds as a practical crop-level propagation method. This regional method is not a seed-starting protocol.

problems.short: Waterleaf can host root-knot nematodes; soggy pots risk root rot
problems.guidance: UF/IFAS describes waterleaf as relatively resistant to pests and diseases but identifies it as a host for root-knot nematode. Singapore NParks advises well-drained, organic loamy potting soil because waterleaf is vulnerable to root rot. These are source-scoped risks, not a diagnosis or a waterleaf-specific treatment prescription. Seed viability and germination are covered separately in Seed Profile.

flowering.short: Pink flowers set small seed capsules; flowering can be observed without assigning a fixed crop calendar
flowering.guidance: UF/IFAS describes pink, bisexual flowers that primarily self-pollinate, with limited outcrossing; it reports fruit ripening about two weeks after flowering. This is species-level reproductive context, not a guarantee of seed set or a home harvest schedule. Seed starting and germination remain in the Seed Profile.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: UF/IFAS describes soil and container culture and does not validate Garden X hydroponic systems.

growthHabits.reason: The source does not map the crop to the controlled system-compatibility habit classes.

height.reason: UF/IFAS height descriptions are not selected as a cultivar-specific indoor mature height.

spread.reason: No reliable indoor mature spread is established.

spacing.reason: Regional soil spacing is not converted to machine pod spacing.

light.reason: Outdoor climate and light context is not translated into an indoor light tier.
